A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of the present study indicate that the psychological functioning of individuals considering genetic counseling and/or testing for Li–fraumeni syndrome (p53) is not significantly different from that of the general population.
the majority of individuals who were at risk for LFS were able to cope with the genetic test results.
the majority of participants were not distressed about cancer or the genetic test and were confident in their ability to cope with the results of genetic testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic testing is a complex decision that should be made by each person at risk, with the help of a trained genetic counselor.
the majority of individuals considering p53 testing for Li–fraumeni syndrome (a hereditary cancer syndrome) do not experience significant psychological distress.
genetic counseling and testing can be a positive experience for some people, and we need more research to better understand why.
